data.body:
Root cause confirmed and fixed in Gerrit change 1647.

MEASURED, not assumed. Against the pre-fix _file_bytes helper, both halves of git
auto-maintenance flip the snapshot comparison:
  - creating .git/objects/maintenance.lock  -> comparison flips (the signature CI saw)
  - git gc repacking loose objects          -> comparison flips, 16 paths differ
    (loose objects collapse into a packfile, .git/info/refs rewritten)

That second limb is the important finding: the narrowest suggested fix in the description
(ignore *.lock under .git/) would NOT have de-flaked this test, because repacking alone is
enough to break it. The oracle's real defect is that it reads git's private storage
representation at all.

FIX: _file_bytes becomes _store_snapshot, which captures (1) every file outside .git/
byte-for-byte and (2) git's LOGICAL ref state -- HEAD plus for-each-ref -- instead of object
bytes. Repacking cannot move a ref so it is invisible; a command that actually committed to
the store moves HEAD and is still caught. The read-only assertion keeps its teeth and loses
its dependence on git's scheduler. Fixture-level maintenance.auto/gc.auto disabling was
rejected: it hides the class rather than fixing the oracle.

RED->GREEN proven, not theoretical. The new regression test
test_store_snapshot_survives_git_maintenance_but_still_catches_mutation fails against the old
helper ('a maintenance lock file is not a store mutation') and passes against the new one. It
covers both maintenance limbs and then asserts the oracle still detects a rewritten payload
file and a HEAD-moving commit, so stability is not bought by going blind. Assertions are
content/ordering facts only; no timing budgets.

Gates: make lint clean, make typecheck clean (503 files), tests/scripts/bridge 87 passed.

SECOND LIMB SPLIT OUT: the sidecar two-clone fixture sync race is a different defect with a
different fix, so it is now willing-cellular-carp, linked discovered_from this ticket.
